# Independent audit of the full-cover joint first-order system

Audited files:

- `candidate de8d1a3251731edd`, Section 5;
- `candidate 0e807db2bba0c137`;
- `candidate cf94bd7190201a57`.

All three pass. This is a mathematical audit of their stated scopes;
no OC inference beyond those scopes is made.

## Joint nonsmooth Fritz--John equations

1. At a unit continuous normal, cap mass is locally Lipschitz in all
   ambient affine coefficients. A small parameter perturbation changes
   membership only in a slab of thickness O(epsilon) on each bounded
   fiber, with a uniformly bounded transverse projection. This remains
   true for d=1 and for cuts supporting a facet.

2. Every generalized cap gradient can be represented by a SINGLE
   consistent collection of densities theta_iz in [0,1] on the limiting
   sections. Nearby nonunit normal factors converge to one. Orthogonal
   projection Jacobians between nearby section planes also converge to
   one. Weak limits retain domination by the limiting section measure
   and support on the actual section; a proper interior section has
   density one. Convex combinations preserve joint mass and first
   moments. This does not claim independent trace choices are feasible.

3. For the active cover constraint, the entire joint gradient depends
   affinely on ONE point of the exposed face minimizing U_z dot x.
   Consequently convexification of these joint gradients still uses
   one point of that same convex face. This includes U_z=0, when the
   exposed face is the whole fiber. The product lambda_zi u_i creates
   no extra first-order term beyond the two components displayed in
   (18): lambda_zi x_z and L_i(z,x_z).

4. The finite separation proof is a valid Fritz--John argument in
   sphere charts and the affine simplex-coordinate hyperplanes. A
   direction strictly decreasing the objective and every active
   generalized inequality gradient would give actual local strict
   improvement. Inactive inequalities persist by continuity. A zero
   convex combination therefore exists. It cannot consist solely of
   active simplex nonnegativity normals: increasing all zero simplex
   coordinates and compensating in one positive coordinate strictly
   improves them in the affine tangent space. Thus the objective,
   budget, and cover multipliers are not all zero. No constraint
   qualification establishing a positive objective multiplier is used.

5. The lambda stationarity signs are correct. For eta_z>0 the selected
   lambda maximizes L_i(z,x_z) over the simplex. Its weighted value is
   C_z=0. Hence every L_i(z,x_z)<=0, and L_i=0 whenever lambda_zi>0.
   Together with exposed-face membership, this proves that the SAME
   point used in the first-order equations is the actual contact.

6. Write c,P,m for cap mass and moments, S,P^s,m^s for effective
   section moments. The unrestricted b and a equations are

       alpha c+rS=sum eta lambda,
       alpha P+rP^s=sum eta lambda z.

   Taking the u inner product of the unsimplified u equation uses

       u.m=Psi+bc-a.P,
       u.m^s=bS-a.P^s,
       lambda>0 => u.x_z=b-a.z.

   All threshold and integer-moment terms cancel, leaving
   sigma=-alpha Psi. This verifies the sign and coefficient one in
   (17). No full ambient coarea factor has been substituted for the
   within-fiber unit-normal factor.

The abnormal case alpha=0 is not merely hypothetical. The companion
note `candidate 2a5e48e3badc4c86`
proves it is forced on every nonregular simplex sharp product.

## Sharp product calibration

The invoked simplex cap-gap theorem counts all vertices in the CLOSED
cap, including boundary vertices. Thus a centroid cap containing at
least two vertices has fraction at least gamma_(d-1)>gamma_d when
d>=2. A one-vertex cap has fraction product(1+b_j)^(-1), with
sum b_j=1, and equality exactly when every b_j=1/d. A cap strictly
containing the centroid loses positive volume when translated to it,
so equality caps must pass through the centroid. The interval case
is explicitly separate.

A budget-saturating cap through one fiber centroid has zero mass in
every other fiber and cannot serve another centroid. The finitely many
caps missing that centroid miss a neighborhood, so the local canonical
caps must cover a neighborhood. Every one of their d+1 types is needed.
The exact count N=2^n(d+1) then forces one of each type in each fiber.

The normalized local margin is H_j(lambda_j-1/(d+1)). Its hinge
integral is v H_j d gamma_d/(d+1)^2. Summing gives the stated formula;
for a regular simplex sum H_j=(d+1)^2 r gives M d r gamma_d.
The explicit binary-tilt construction is finite, has the exact cap
budget, and covers all boundary points. No limiting halfspace or
boundary-mass interchange occurs.

## Positive inradius below maximum balanced mass

For 0<s<min(t,w), the translated homothet
(1-theta)p+theta K with theta=(s/w)^(1/d) has exactly volume s and
is contained in K. Its centroids give the claimed translated copy of
(1-theta)K inside the trimmed centroid body.

Mixing an attained mass-T balanced submeasure with any such mass-s
fiber submeasure by coefficients (t-s)/(T-s) and (T-t)/(T-s)
preserves domination, gives mass t, and keeps integer centroid j.
Dividing its continuous moment by t gives exactly the factor
(T-t)s/[t(T-s)]. Every denominator is positive. The resulting radius
is positive for all 0<t<T, and the advertised choices t=D_j/2 and
s=min(D_j/4,w/2) satisfy every strict inequality because T>=D_j>=w>0.
The inherited cover-hinge inequality therefore has the stated positive
right side without an additional inball hypothesis on the moment body.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
